title: Why did Eliot Ness let a suspected serial killer walk free?
description:
In 1935, two boys discovered headless, drained bodies in Cleveland's Kingsbury Run, kicking off a terrifying spree of twelve dismembered victims. Despite 'surgical precision' cuts and an investigation led by Eliot Ness—the man who took down Al Capone—only three victims were ever identified.

The prime suspect was Dr. Francis Sweeney, a surgeon who failed a lie detector test spectacularly. But because his cousin was a sitting congressman, Ness never charged him. Instead, police beat a false confession out of a laborer who died in his cell, while Sweeney spent decades mailing taunting postcards to Ness from an asylum.

Who was the real Mad Butcher of Kingsbury Run? Subscribe now 👇
